title: Junior capital sourced by spending SPJ capacity permanently carries a Senior-Per-Junior ratio of zero, cutting off recursive leverage
content:
A.3.2.1.2.3 states the purpose of the sourcing ratios: ensuring a Prime Agent holds appropriate Internal Junior Risk Capital "relative to its External and Senior capital exposures, ensuring sufficient 'skin in the game.'" Two ratios do the work, applied in a fixed order per A.3.2.1.2.3.2.

First, the **External Per Internal (EPI)** ratio caps how much external junior capital (rented PEJRC plus tokenized TEJRC) an Agent may source, "based solely on the Prime Agent's IJRC" — its own capital is the only anchor. Second, the **Senior Per Junior (SPJ)** ratio is applied to the resulting junior pool (IJRC plus EPI-sourced EJRC) to compute how much Senior Risk Capital that junior layer can "enable." A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2 makes enablement binding: an Agent "might hold a certain amount of OSRC or rented SRC, but only the portion that is successfully 'enabled' by its JRC according to the SPJ ratios" counts toward its Required Risk Capital.

A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2.1 then adds flexibility — SPJ capacity may instead be spent to source *additional* external junior capital beyond what EPI alone allows — and immediately closes the loop it would otherwise open: "the EJRC tranche acquired through utilizing SPJ capacity is permanently accounted for as having an SPJ ratio of zero (0). It contributes to the JRC buffer but provides no capacity itself for enabling SRC in any subsequent calculations."

Without that zero, the structure would be recursive: junior capital generates SPJ capacity, SPJ capacity buys more junior capital, which generates more capacity — a geometric series limited only by the ratio's value. Marking SPJ-sourced capital as permanently sterile makes the cascade exactly two steps deep, so total leverage stays a bounded multiple of the Agent's own capital.

A.3.2.1.2.3.2 adds the non-double-spend rule: "Any specific portion of the total SPJ capacity allocated towards sourcing EJRC cannot simultaneously be allocated towards enabling SRC." The Agent gets a genuine choice between a thicker first-loss buffer and more senior capacity, but not both from the same capacity.
description: Capital sourcing runs EPI on internal capital, then SPJ capacity on the resulting junior pool; SPJ capacity may be spent on senior enablement or extra junior capital, but never compounded twice.
